entries.claim: Port-mismatch protection can be bypassed by changing only the case of the persisted hostname.
entries.failure_scenario: Set `git.forge_host` to `Forge.Example.COM:3001` (accepted by `splitForgeHost`), then run `create` with `--remote-url https://forge.example.com/o/r.git`. `classifyOrigin` lowercases the URL host to `forge.example.com`, but `instance.hostname` remains `Forge.Example.COM`, so the exact case-sensitive comparison fails. The command proceeds to create the repository and wires an HTTPS origin on default port 443 rather than the configured instance port 3001, precisely the destructive wrong-origin outcome this check is intended to prevent.

entries.claim: The hostname grammar enforces only the total DNS-name length and accepts invalid overlong DNS labels.
entries.failure_scenario: `git.forge_host=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.example.com:3001` is accepted: its total length is below 253 and the 64-character first label matches `HOST_LABEL`. DNS labels are limited to 63 octets, so this accepted persisted Forgejo address cannot be resolved as a DNS hostname; later `tea` login/API operations against it fail even though config set/check/validate reported the value as valid. The included acceptance of `'h'.repeat(253)` codifies the same invalid single-label case.
